unit.title: 3D Shapes
unit.blurb: Nets of cubes and other solids, counting faces, edges and vertices, and drawing and recognising 3D shapes from different views.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Identify and sketch different nets for a cube and other simple 3D shapes.

O2.t: Describe 3D shapes by their faces, edges and vertices, and recognise them from drawings and views.

p: A **net** is a flat shape that folds up to make a 3D shape. A cube has **6 square faces**, so every net of a cube is made of 6 squares.
There are **11** different nets of a cube. Some arrangements of 6 squares do NOT fold into a cube because two faces would overlap.
Five squares in a row cannot fold into a cube: the end squares overlap.

p: A **face** is a flat or curved surface, an **edge** is where two faces meet and a **vertex** is a corner.
A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. On isometric (dotty) paper we can draw 3D shapes so they look solid.
Some edges are hidden at the back. Dashed lines show them.
